question: Does dedicated full-three-view readout training improve over matched subset-readout training, and does cross-user supervised contrast add value beyond ordinary SupCon?
input: verified per-fold multiview_s2026 features [9300,3,256]; original encoder is frozen and is not retrained
split: test H, validation H%8+1, other six users train; original quality mask and IDs
model: Linear(771,256), GELU, Dropout(0.1), Linear(256,12); three physical feature slots plus three observation flags; exact original fusion-head topology
feature_scaling: none; retain exported input representation for every arm
sampler: two distinct examples per available train user-class cell in each batch, shuffled; identical epoch sampling across arms; ceil(train_count / cell_count / 2) steps per epoch
subset_ce: one uniform nonempty physical-view subset per batch; zero unavailable features, explicit flags; all seven subsets known in advance
full_arms: all three physical views for every training and evaluation sample
selection: earliest minimum full-view validation CE, including epoch 0, for every arm

supcon.crossuser_denominator: different-class samples and same-class different-user samples; self and same-class same-user samples excluded

continue_criterion: full_crossuser exceeds full_ce, full_supcon and historical LTR by at least 1 percentage point mean user macro accuracy, and improves full_ce on at least 6/8 users
second_seed_rule: only if continuation criterion is met; repeat matched arms at seed2027 without changing configuration
test_policy: test labels used only for post-selection metrics; all eight test users already have exploration history
limits: Not an end-to-end reproduction; no old encoder weights in transfer. Improvements over cached historical LTR cannot be attributed solely to subset sampling, because historical optimizer and sampling differ. Use matched subset_ce vs full_ce for that narrower contrast. This is a necessary baseline/mechanism check, not a new architecture or established paper contribution.
